Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8159094
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/14/2023
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after a truck roll over caused produced fluid to be released along the access road on August 30, 2023. In an email sent to the Department by EQT representative Rick Hall on 9/5/23, he relayed that excavation was complete on the area impacted by the release along the access road. He said that the area of the impact had been delineated by environmental consultant Penn E and R using field instrumentation. He also stated that impacted material which had been excavated was staged within secondary containment on Pad A. Trees have been cleared from the area of the truck rollover on the west side of the access road as well as the area east of the NFG pipeline right-of-way at the north stormwater culvert. The full excavated area has been temporarily stabilized. No fluid was observed in the excavated area. Compost filter sock has been installed as appropriate around the excavated area. No E and S issues noted.On Pad B, nine wells are staged for production. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the sump at the east end of the north stormwater channel was 1800 uS/cm. On Pad A, excavated material is tarped and sits within secondary containment. Six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment and they appear to be in good condition. Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release from the MASS on 12/19/22.

Comments: On 4/27/2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection of well 1M at the Hephaestus well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. Present were Rosie Wise (DEP Environmental Trainee) and myself.An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP-3) was issued by the Department for this site on May 27, 2020 and expired on May 26, 2025. On May 1, 2025, this site was added to the Department's Extended NOT Program, extending the ESCGP expiration date to August 26, 2025 (see IR 3969339). Violations were issued in IR 4043991 against the expired ESCGP, for failure to maintain PCSM BMP's, and failure to have site permanently stabilized.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and the Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) inspection log are onsite. The ERP appears to contain the sections required by 78a.55. The remaining documents on site were not evaluated due to the mailbox being infested by insects. The DEP recommends that the operator ensure continued safe accessibility of the on-site documentation. The PPC plan appeared to contain the sections required by 78a.55 at the time of IR 4167813 (photos 2-4). Six gas wells are onsite that appear to be equipped for production (photo 12). No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the gas wells. The well tag has detached from well 1M (photos 13 and 14).The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 5, 6, and 8). An area observed adjacent to the soil stockpile along the access road exhibits less than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage (photo 7). The Department recommends that the operator mulch and seed this location.The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection. The GPU units and Dehy unit are placed on raised secondary containment skids, with no fluid leaks observed (photos 9-11).Based on observations from this inspection, a violation shall be issued for failure to install the API number to well 1M in a permanent manner.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/28/2021 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Monroe Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/27/2021
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 940411
Permit API: 015-22501
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Monroe Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/28/2021
Comments: Eric Hottenstein (Chesapeake) notified Carrie Knapp (NCRO) that at 1530 hrs Monday December 27, 2021 they discovered approximately 112 barrels of produced water/freshwater spilled. A flowback tank in containment leaked, and the containment leaked onto the pad. (CTS 361265). I spoke with William Dolan (Creston Environmental LLC) on site. He explained they are using a YSI meter and a soil probe to delineate the extent of the reported 112 barrel brine/freshwater mix release to the pad surface which occurred yesterday. A vac truck with a T adapter (photo) is removing that liquid from the pad surface. A track hoe (photo) is removing the impacted pad soil/rock and loading into a dump-truck. The truck then dumps the material on liner containment (photo) on the opposite side of the pad. I used an Oakton PCSTestr 35 to get electrical conductivity (EC) readings from pooled liquid on the pad surface. In the area where the release occurred, it gave readings of 8.0-12.2 mS/cm. I collected liquid sample 0935-429 from the area that was 12.2 mS/cm. Pooled liquid on the pad surface unaffected by the release is 0.16-0.22 mS/cm. I also used a Hanna soil probe to get EC readings from the pad material. In the excavated area it gave a 0.04 mS/cm reading; the unexcavated area immediately outside it gave readings of 3.0-4.0 mS/cm. 4.0 mS /cm is the max limit for the Hanna soil probe. The EC readings indicate the brine release did not flow outside of the pad surface. Rock, vegetation, and straw mulch stabilize soil of the site. I did not observe accelerated erosion or sedimentation. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Cleanup of this spill will be referred to the DEP ECB program for Act 2 compliance. Air temp 40F JLP

Violation ID: 8284092
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2026
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document a field review of the recent removal of grub material previously located between the proposed Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads. William Cenk and Brian Bennett of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) were present for the duration of this inspection. Brian Ayers (WQSS) and I, Mathew Haemer (WQS), were present to represent the Department.During the 07/21/26 JPA pre-application meeting between TMP and the Department, Department Technical Services staff requested that the grub material placed south of the roadway between the Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads be removed as soon as possible to potentially restore the hydrology near the road and well pad construction back to its original condition. It was observed that the grub material had impeded and redirected the flow of an Unnamed Tributary to Jackson Run and had begun to cause E and S problems alongside the roadway, well pad, and below the well pad for the proposed Akins #4 conventional well.At the time of this inspection, it appeared that all of the grub material had been removed as requested. However, TMP had also elected to redefine one of the stream channels below the well pad for Akins #3 and direct its flow through the disturbed area south of the roadway to Akins #4. The excavation work related to this stream channel continues to cause erosion and sedimentation to occur alongside the roadway and well pad for the proposed Akins #4. This is not the outcome Technical Services staff intended to result from the removal of the grub material. At the time of this inspection, the newly excavated stream channel is unprotected from erosion. There are three filter socks installed south of the Akins #4 well pad beyond the excavated stream channel directly in line with this channelized flow. Filter sock is not designed to be installed in channelized flow. All three filter socks are being undercut by the channelized flow. Evidence of erosion and sedimentation is still present before and after each filter sock. The area south and continuing west of Akins #4 that is now accepting the flow of this stream water is beginning to erode. A forested wetland is located west and down grade from the Akins #4 well pad. Bank erosion and saturated earth below the wetland indicate that the stream water overflows the wetland during storm events.The Department has yet to receive an updated E and S Plan that meets the expectations of the Technical Services staff. It is recommended that no further earth disturbance occurs without notification to and approval by the Department.The encroachment violations and violations relating to erosion and sediment control continue in the present condition of this construction and related excavation work.The violation for failure to post the well permit during construction has been closed.

Comments: On April 14, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection in response to the operator's submission of a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug this well.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. During today's inspection, the following was observed:- E and S Plan is present on-site- Site is adequately vegetated at this time.- No E and S issues are observed on site at this time. - CFS has been installed on-site in accordance with the plans, however the CFS is not installed properly as the upslope side does not include chinking. - RCE has not been installed on-site in accordance with the E and S Plan and the construction sequence, which calls for RCE to be installed prior to CFS.- Tire tracks are observed near the area that is suspected to be the permitted location of the RCE (Photo 23) as this location is moderately saturated. - Well tag and posting requirements are not met on site (Photos 10, 11, 19) despite two postings present. One posting includes the incorrect API number and belongs to a previous operator. The second posting does not include the API number or the operator's address.- Production tank is present on-site and is surrounded by an earthen berm. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed on site at this time. Violations are being issued for well tag and posting requirements not met on site, improperly installed E and S BMPs, and for failure to construct the site in accordance with the E and S Plan.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/6/2023 at 1430 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by Blackhill. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #371191 is tied to this release within CTS. On 4/6/2023 at ~1300 hours an initial estimate of 4 barrels of produced water was discovered by Blackhill Energy to have been released from the produced water offload area at the Jackson pad. Prior to my arrival, the estimate was increased to a potential 7 barrels of produced water. The release occurred when the offload valve for the produced water tanks was not closed all the way after offloading. The valve is held in a yellow bin and the produced water was discovered to be leaking from the bin shown in photo #2. As it leaked from the bin, part of the release was contained to secondary containment and part of the release was spilled to the pad surface. During my inspection, fluids located on the pad surface in the known impacted area from the release were field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photos #1 and 2). After inspecting the rock-lined conveyance channel located just west of the release area (photo #4) it was discovered that elevated conductivity fluids were located in the channel. I field measured fluids in the rock-lined conveyance channel along the entirety of the southern edge of the pad. All fluids in the rock-lined channel up to the stormwater control basin were field measured at >19.99mS/cm. Fluid flowing in the rock-lined channel was observed entering the stormwater control basin. I collected a sample (0983-377) for standard analysis code 942 from the fluid located in the rock-lined conveyance channel just before entering the stormwater control basin (photo #11). This fluid was field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photo #10). Two sumps were constructed along the rock-lined channel to begin collecting any fluids flowing in the channel. The DEP requested that the now impacted stormwater contained in the stormwater basin be collected as a regulated substance due to the release impacting it. As I departed a crew were working on excavating the impacted pad material near the point of release and recovering the fluids that were on the surface of the pad. Temporary storage containers were scheduled to be brought in to be staged onsite for storage of the stormwater control basin's water. Plans to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment to begin excavating beneath it were also being made. The drain pipe of the stormwater basin was believed to be clogged but was also closed as a precaution. I departed the site at 1600 hours. Based on the reported release of produced water outside of containment and the discovery of the release entering conveyance channels and reaching the stormwater controls, violations of the following are cited against API #015-23733: 25 Pa. Some scraping and removal of pad material around the western corner of the pad surface has been conducted. Materials removed from the pad and soils removed from impacted areas downslope are being stored within a secondary containment structure on the pad (photo #1). Repsol has obtained approval to dispose of impacted materials at a landfill. A rain event occurred on Thursday, 7/31/2025. A crew worked today to install a 4-inch line that will eventually pump fluids collected in the lined detention basin into a storage tank held on the pad surface. Fluids will only be held in the 4-inch line when pumping from the basin is ongoing. Three shallow, monitoring wells have been drilled downslope of the well pad to monitor the groundwater (see photo #14 for example). Comments: On 8/10/23 at 1201 hrs., I conducted an incident inspection of Madtick Development Corp.'s Musser Associates 2 well site (API 063-32934) in East Mahoning Twp., Indiana Co. The inspection was conducted in response to a phone call received on 8/10/23 from the landowner, indicating that a production fluid release was observed at the well site. The landowner unsuccessfully attempted to contact the operator, and then reported the release to the Department. Upon inspection of the site, stressed/dead vegetation was observed around the production fluid tank onsite, and in an adjacent corn field. The area of dead vegetation appears to be approximately 30-45 feet wide and extends approximately 200-250 feet to the North of the well site. The release appears to be originating from a tank onsite. The tank appears to be empty. The release appears to be over 1 barrel of fluid. In addition to the release, it was observed that the well is equipped for production. A well tag is not affixed to the completed well. A site ID sign is posted, but is illegible and does not display the required information.Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), and 78.66(b) are being cited for failure by the operator to report the release, and are immediately being closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of OGA 3211(G) and OGA 3211(H) are cited for the lack of site ID sign and well tag. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1) are cited for the release of production fluids from the tank onto the ground. The violations will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release anddemonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.

The fluid in the sump has an electrical conductivity (EC) of 2.07 mS/cm. A visible path was observed from the northeast edge of the sump to the farthest line of compost filter sock near the site limit-of-distance (LOD). This had not been observed in any previous inspection. Mr. Subra took an EC reading of the soil at the end of the path in front of the compost filter sock and it was 300 uS/cm. Multiple puddles of fluid were found north and northwest of the MASS. The EC of this fluid ranged from 2.62 mS/cm to 7.70 mS/cm. I took sample number 0718-199 from the puddles northwest of the mass and north of the secondary containment for the parking area of the super sucker vacuum truck.The fluid in the containment to the east of the MASS is approximately 2 mS/cm. The Department recommends emptying the containment. A line that brings fluid from the gas busters at the produced fluid offload area and puts it into the MASS appeared to still have a slow leak. A tray was underneath this area along the line which had what appeared to be an oily substance in it. The Department recommends ensuring that this does not leak onto the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming up any and all puddles found in the vicinity of the MASS until the 12/19/22 release is remediated. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum out the sump at the end of the stormwater channel. The Department recommends repairing or replacing the line of damaged compost filter sock near the sump. The Department recommends reporting any additional developments regarding the MASS release to the Department including elevated electrical conductivity puddles found in a new area on the pad surface. Violations remain outstanding for the 12/19/22 reported release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad B.

Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on the site following the discovery of fluid with electrical conductivity above 8 mS/cm on the well pad on January 22, 2026. The site was snow-covered during this inspection. Nine wells are staged for production on the well pad. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. Two dehydrators are present within secondary containment. The dehydrators and containment appear to be in good condition.Fluid was present on the pad surface in the offload area of the south frac tank battery. The fluid had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 7.63 mS/cm to 15.47 mS/cm. Inside the secondary containment for the frac tank battery, fluid was present with an EC of >19.99 mS/cm. The EC of the fluid was consistently >19.99 mS/cm in all areas within the secondary containment. I took Sample 0718-268 from the fluid inside the secondary containment at 1440. The sample was sent to the state laboratory on the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Al, Li, Br. I called Rick Hall of EQT on the same day at 1553. I told him about my findings relating to the fluid on the pad surface and within the secondary containment. I asked him if any remediation had been performed for the puddles discovered on the pad surface on 1/22/26. He stated that the fluid has been continuously vacuumed up from this area of the well pad but no excavation had been performed. He said that a couple of days earlier, a contractor had reported the release of a few gallons of produced fluid from a failed bleeder valve into the containment. In a voicemail from 2/10/26, Mr. Hall stated that they excavated the area of the pad surface in the offload area for the south frac tank. That material was containerized for disposal. He stated that the containment was being cleaned out as well and the secondary containment would be extended out so that trucks offloading will be fully on containment while they offload.Violations remain outstanding. The analytical results of Sample 0718-267 taken from the pad surface in the south frac tank battery offload area have still not been received. The violations may be closed or additional violations may be added pending the receipt of the sample results.

properties.content:

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 4/04/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to the report of a discharge of crude oil from this well on April 2, 2022. The release occurred as a result of vandalism, in which a third party individual who had climbed the pump jack damaged a valve on the gathering lime riser when jumping off of the jack. Pennsylvania State Police investigated the incident and the responsible party was found and reportedly admitted what had happened. Upon my arrival, repairs have been made and there was no active discharge. The majority of the released product remained on the well site and a portion of the spur road leading to it. The contaminated soil/rock from the location and road (approximately 3-5 tons) has been excavated and placed on a contained pit liner for upcoming disposal. There was no evidence that any of the released product entered the road ditch that runs alongside the spur road. No watercourses were impacted as a result of this incident. Crews were in the process of removing oil soaked leaves along the edge of the road/location. After that work is completed, no additional remediation measures appear necessary, as the ground underneath the leaves does not appear to be impacted per field screening. A future inspection will be conducted to evaluate if any additional measures are necessary.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8236731

Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Foster Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/04/2025
Comments: This follow-up inspection is being conducted to evaluate First America Energy's (FAE) compliance with the October 28, 2024 Consent Order and Agreement (COA) entered into and agreed upon by FAE and the Department. As referenced in the Department's findings under Paragraph G of the COA, a January 3, 2024 inspection with violations (Record No. 3669334) of the Warrant 4917 4917 156 well site and Tank Battery documented evidence of production fluid discharges from the Tank Battery. Elevated specific conductance of standing fluids and soils were observed within the secondary containment area along its western wall, and outside of the secondary containment area beginning at its northern corner.The corrective actions that were agreed to by FAE pertaining to the release of fluids at the Warrant 4917 4917 156 well site and tank battery are outlined under Paragraph 3.b. of the COA.The Department received a written plan from FAE on December 19, 2024. FAE's written plan entails the use of a "mini excavator which will be used to dig small test holes around the release area to determine a perimeter. FAE will determine this parameter by utilizing a probe to test the conductivity of the soil. During this testing, any soil measuring greater than 1,000 micro siemens will be considered contaminated, any soil less than 1,000 micro siemens will be considered clean" (December 19, 2024 written plan). From there, FAE's plan indicates their intention to hire a contractor to remove all soils with elevated specific conductance and backfill the excavated area with native soils.At the time of this inspection, no visual evidence of remediation work can be observed at the Tank Battery. The evidence of production fluid discharge along the western wall of the secondary containment and outside of the secondary containment beginning at its northern corner is visible via areas of no/stressed vegetation, and pooled fluids with elevated specific conductance. Increased deer activity can also be observed in these areas. Pooled fluid atop the affected area within the secondary containment along its western wall was observed to have specific conductance in excess of 1,000 microSiemens per centimeter.There is no evidence of replacement or improvement to the secondary containment, as ordered by Paragraph 3.b.v. of the COA.At the time of this inspection, the Department has not received a Final Report from FAE.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Eqt Production Co
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2018-12-17

Permit API: 059-27170
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2018-12-17
Comments: On 12/16/18 at approximately 0715 a water truck at the site rolled off the access road, causing an impaired water release. According to Oil & Gas Inspector Supervisor Scott Sabocheck's Emergency Response Team report, approximately 110 barrels of produced fluid and approximately 100-130 gallons of diesel fuel were released to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth. EQT reported the release to the Department at 0745. On 12/17/18 at approximately 1050 hours I conducted an incident response inspection. I met with David Guidas of EQT who explained that a water truck was on its way to the AST with a load of impaired water when it got too close to the edge of the access road and rolled over the edge onto water lines servicing the AST and frack. The spill occurred in a sediment trap, limiting the extent of the spill. Due to the presence of rain water in the sediment trap the spill impacted Waters of the Commonwealth. Approximately 90 barrels of rain water, impaired water, and diesel fuel were recovered by a vac truck. SPSI had conducted remediation of the spill at the time of investigation. Guidas indicated additional screenings were to be conducted and further excavation, as water with elevated conductivity was still being observed. Guidas indicated once the final remediation was complete Corey Giles of EQT would be handling the Act 2 process. OGIS Sabocheck indicated in his ERT report that EQT agreed to pressure test the lines prior to placing the damaged lines back in use. At the time of inspection David Guidas of EQT indicated a section of line had been replaced.

Violation ID: 8168985
Permit API: 125-22304
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2023
Comments: On December 12 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Cole 1 OG Well in response to IR 3641696.The findings are as follows: The area of a leak around the production tank previously observed appeared to have undergone remediation activities. It appeared impacted soil had been removed and filled in with a fine, light colored material. This fine, light colored material appeared to be holding an excess amount of water resulting in the ground surrounding the production tank to be soft and not properly stabilized. The Department attempted to take conductivity readings of the soil but was unable to dig below the newly placed material as it was so saturated it filled any holes dug back in. Conductivity readings of new material were taken with readings of 0.23mS and 0.35mS. Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted KPI Representative Joel Greco to inquire about the remediation efforts and saturated material around the production tank resulting in improper stabilization. Mr.Greco stated they remediated the site by removing almost 3 tons of impacted material. This material is now being stored off site, awaiting sampling to determine how to dispose of it. He also stated that the fine, light color material is a fine limestone material that was placed in the area of excavation. He insured that the material would stabilize after it dries once, allowing it to compact. Based on today's inspection, violations associated with the spill remain open as the remediation efforts are still being reviewed by the Department. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending a follow up inspection.

Comments: On March 2, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4128962.The Department and the Operator entered into a COA for this site in March 7, 2019.E and S Plans on-site are not updated as discussed in IR 4128962. The Department requested new E and S phase and Restoration phase drawings added to the plan set to include the rough delineation of the wetland. The Department also requested adding a wetland seed mix to the delineated wetland, which has also not been added to the plan set. CFS near the access road entrance and stockpile along the access road appear to have been impacted by truck traffic. The Department recommends the operator maintain the CFS and ensure it is installed properly. No E and S issues are observed at this time.Orange construction fence has been installed surrounding the flowing surface water from the wetland. Operator has added compost chinking to the existing CFS on-site. No additional CFS appears to have been installed at this time. CFS surrounding the site and wetland appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time. No E and S issues are observed at this time. What appears to be absorbent pads are observed within the flowing water on site (Photos 14-16, 22). Specific conductivity was recorded for background and within the area of the absorbent pads to assess for possible spill. The Department did not observe elevated specific conductivity readings or a sheen in the water near the pads. However the Department requests a response with information on why the absorbent pads are located within the water on site.The pipe identified in IRs 4125575 and 4128962 appears to have been removed as described by the operator in the NOV response. As requested in IR 4128962, the Department requests a written response to include any findings regarding the pipe, including the size of the pipe, use, and if it was connected to additional equipment. Violations remain outstanding at this time. The Department requests the plan set be updated and a written response be received by the Department by March 16, 2026.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 12/14/2022
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 978577
Permit API: 005-29235
Unconventional: No
County: Armstrong
Municipality: Gilpin Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/14/2022
Comments: On Wednesday, 12/14/2022, I conducted a routine inspection of the Diversified Production, LLC McIntyre 1 well, permit number 005-29235. The well is located in the woods off of Coal Bank Road in Gilpin township, Armstrong county. The well is in production and had a reported production of 5,341.89 mcf for 2021. There is a well id tag attached to the well head and a well site id sign is posted on the production chart box. The site is restored, but the operator has not maintained the E and S BMP's for the site and there is an area of standing/ponded water on the access road near the site entrance (see picture #8) that needs to be addressed. The site cannot be considered stabilized due to this area and also the area of dead vegetation that was caused by brine being sprayed from a broken pipe onto the brine tank and ground. The brine tank itself is stable and appears to be structurally sound, but the pipe into the brine tank from the gas separator has rusted through and broken off, spraying brine onto the outside of the tank and onto the ground (see pictures #6 and #7). The amount of brine released appears to be less than 1 bbl. These conditions have resulted in violations to 25 PA Code 78.57(a), 25 PA Code 78.54, SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1) and CSL 402(b) being cited. Although there were no violations cited, the deficiencies on the access road need to be addressed while the operator is addressing the conditions that resulted in the cited violations.
